'''Paolo Giuseppe Radaelli''', [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics|FInstP]] (born 11 October 1961) is an Italian [[physicist]] and academic. He is the [[Dr Lee's Professor of Experimental Philosophy ]] (Physics) at the [[University of Oxford]] and a [[Fellow (Oxbridge)|Professorial Fellow]] of [[Wadham College, Oxford]].<ref name="Wadham">{{cite web |url=https://www.wadham.ox.ac.uk/people/fellows-and-academic-staff/r/paolo-radaelli |title=Paolo Radaelli |publisher=[[Wadham College, Oxford]] |accessdate=2017-07-27 |archive-date=11 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170911061146/http://www.wadham.ox.ac.uk/people/fellows-and-academic-staff/r/paolo-radaelli |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="WW17">'RADAELLI, Prof. Paolo Giuseppe', ''[[Who's Who 2017]]'', A & C Black, an imprint of Bloomsbury Publishing plc, 2017; online edn, Oxford University Press, 2016; online edn, Nov 2016 [http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U253939 accessed 27 July 2017]</ref>

== Biography ==
Radaelli obtained a Laurea degree ''Summa cum Laude'' in 1986 from [[University of Milan]] (his thesis supervisor was Pino Marchesini). As part of the mandatory Italian National Service, he served for one year in the {{ill|28º Reggimento "Pavia"|it|vertical-align=sup}} as a drill instructor, leaving with the rank of corporal major. Between 1988 and 1989, he worked as a research associate at the ITM institute of the [[National Research Council (Italy)]] in the field of [[High-temperature superconductivity]]. In 1989, he was awarded a travel scholarship by [[Pirelli Cavi e Sistemi]] and moved to the [[Illinois Institute of Technology]] (Chicago), where he later completed a PhD under the academic supervision of Carlo Segre, and worked in close collaboration with James D. Jorgensen and David Hinks at [[Argonne National Laboratory]]. After a post-doc in Jorgensen's group between 1992 and 1993, he moved to Grenoble, first as a post-doc with Massimo Marezio at the Laboratories de Cristallographie of the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]], then as a scientist at the [[Institut Laue–Langevin]]. In 1998, he became an Instrument Scientists and later Crystallography Group Leader at the [[ISIS neutron source]] at the [[Rutherford Appleton Laboratory]] in Didcot, England. Since 2008, he has been the [[Dr Lee's Professor of Experimental Philosophy]] (Physics) at the [[University of Oxford]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=From rust to riches? Computing goes green...or is that brown? {{!}} University of Oxford |url=https://www.ox.ac.uk/news/science-blog/rust-riches-computing-goes-greenor-brown |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=www.ox.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref> and he is also a [[Fellow (Oxbridge)|Professorial Fellow]] of [[Wadham College, Oxford]]. In 2017, he was appointed a Knight of the [[Order of the Star of Italy]].<ref name="Star">{{cite web|url=http://www.amblondra.esteri.it/ambasciata_londra/en/ambasciata/ufficio-stampa/news/2017/07/professore-paolo-radaelli-conferimento.html|title=Paolo Radaelli is made a Knight of the Order of the Star of Italy|date=2017-07-13|work=News|publisher=[[Embassy of Italy, London]]|accessdate=2017-07-27}}</ref>
